input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: the walk over exc.__cause__ has no cycle guard, so a chain that loops back on itself never reaches None
- failure path: an exception raised with `raise e from e`, or two exceptions that cause each other, makes retry_if_exception_cause_type spin forever at full CPU; the stop conditions never run and the caller hangs

Reviewer finding
- description: The cycle-detection guard (`seen` set) was removed from the `__cause__` chain walk, so the loop can now run forever if the chain contains a cycle.
- rationale: Trigger: a retried function raises an exception whose `__cause__` chain loops back on itself, e.g. `a.__cause__ = b; b.__cause__ = a`, and no exception in the chain matches `exception_cause_types`. The loop `while exc is not None` then never reaches None, so the retry predicate never returns and the caller hangs at 100% CPU instead of retrying or raising.
critique: The finding describes the same defect: the `__cause__` chain walk has no cycle guard, so a cyclic chain never reaches None. The predicate then loops forever and the caller hangs at full CPU. It points at the same loop and gives the same trigger, mutually causing exceptions.
